validate.title: Validate your e-invoice - jasy
validate.description: Check any ZUGFeRD or XRechnung invoice against the KoSIT EN 16931 rules and veraPDF - free, from any tool. The file is checked and deleted at once, nothing is stored.
validate.label: free validator · official rules · nothing stored
validate.intro: jasy generates ZUGFeRD and XRechnung e-invoices in pure TypeScript. You shouldn't take our word that they're conformant, so don't. Drop in {any} e-invoice below, made by any tool, and check it against the official rules: KoSIT's EN 16931 business rules and veraPDF, the reference validator for PDF/A.
validate.outro: This is the exact check jasy runs on every invoice it generates. Build conformant e-invoices in pure TypeScript.

footer.tagline: PDFs and ZUGFeRD / XRechnung e-invoices in pure TypeScript, with no headless browser and no Java.
footer.built: Built with Nuxt · self-hosted fonts · no trackers

validator.dropHint: A ZUGFeRD or XRechnung PDF (or the raw XML), made by any tool. Or click to choose.
validator.privacy: processed in memory · never stored · deleted instantly
validator.errorUnreachable: We couldn't reach the validator. Please try again in a moment.
validator.errorSample: Couldn't load the sample invoice. Please try again.
validator.invalid: Not valid · {n} issue | Not valid · {n} issues
validator.footnote: Validated with veraPDF, the PDF Association's official open-source PDF/A validator, and the EN 16931 (KoSIT) business rules. jasy only runs them - the verdict is theirs.

hero.lead: Write components, get paper - and {einvoices} that pass the official EN 16931 and PDF/A checks. The engine is our own - no headless browser, no Java - and draws PDFs in Node or right in the browser.
hero.asideText: Validate any ZUGFeRD or XRechnung PDF, even ones jasy didn't make, against veraPDF and the official EN 16931 rules. Nothing stored.

einvoice.lead: One typed object in, a conformant e-invoice out: the PDF a person reads and the EN 16931 data a machine reads. Java has Mustangproject, PHP has horstoeko/zugferd, Python has factur-x - this is the TypeScript answer.
einvoice.p1Text: Line nets, totals and the VAT breakdown are computed from your data - nothing typed twice, nothing off by a cent.
einvoice.p2Text: PDF/A-3 with the EN 16931 XML inside, or the XML alone - CII or UBL, one switch.
einvoice.p3Text: No service, no upload, no Java. It runs in your Node process, next to your data.

trust.label: why trust it
trust.title: Every claim on this page links to its proof.
trust.engineText: Layout, text shaping and the PDF writer are ours, in TypeScript. No Chromium, no Java, no pdf-lib underneath.
trust.speedText: Six documents against react-pdf, pdfmake and jsPDF - same text, same pages, harness in the repo.
trust.checkedText: E-invoices pass the KoSIT EN 16931 rules and veraPDF. Check any file yourself - ours or anyone's.
trust.a11yText: One flag emits a tagged PDF/UA-1 document that passes veraPDF's machine checks.
trust.bytesText: The same document renders to the same bytes, every time - an archived invoice stays reproducible.
trust.anywhereText: Node or the browser, plain TypeScript, Vue, React or Nuxt - the same engine underneath.

runtimes.lead: Pure TypeScript, no Node-only crutches. The same component tree produces the same byte-exact PDF whether it runs on a server or entirely in the browser - your call, not the library's.
runtimes.serverText: Generate invoices and reports in your API or backend - dependency-light, no Chromium to boot, no JVM to feed.
runtimes.browserText: Render the whole PDF in the user's browser - no server round-trip, works offline, and nothing ever leaves the device.

vue.label: PDFs as Vue components
vue.lead: Author a document the way you build an app - components, props, slots and your reactive data - then render it to a real PDF, right in the browser. Real layout and pagination underneath, fully typed props, and a familiar feel if you have reached for {reactPdf} on the React side.
vue.inBrowser: // → a PDF, right in the browser
vue.p1Text: Author a document the way you build an app - reusable components, props and slots.
vue.p2Text: Your reactive data drives the page; loops, conditions and computed values just work.
vue.p3Text: The isomorphic engine turns the component tree into a PDF client-side - no server required.

react.label: PDFs as React components
react.lead: Author a document in JSX - components, props, hooks and context - then render it to a real PDF, right in the browser. Real layout and pagination underneath: tables that carry their header across pages, newspaper columns, headers and footers that keep their space.
react.inBrowser: // → a PDF, right in the browser
react.p1Text: Author a document the way you build an app - props, hooks, context and your own components.
react.p2Text: Every prop is the engine's own option type, so every option autocompletes the day it ships.
react.p3Text: The isomorphic engine turns the element tree into a PDF client-side - or on a server, the same call.

nuxt.label: the Nuxt module
nuxt.lead: One install, zero config. Author PDFs as components and render them right in the browser, or stream them from a server route - your choice, the same components and helpers on both sides.
nuxt.p1Text: Add it to modules. Components and the render helpers are auto-imported - no wiring, no imports.
nuxt.p2Text: Render in the browser with usePdf, or stream from a Nitro route with definePdfHandler. Same vocabulary.
nuxt.p3Text: Cache a route per path + query in one option. jimp stays server-side - the browser bundle stays small.

roadmap.lead: Built in the open, MIT-licensed. Everything the 1.0 set out to do is done and shipping; this is what comes after it - in order, no dates promised.
roadmap.editText: Open a file, change what is on the page, and merge, split or extract. Reading a form and filling it already ships.
roadmap.signText: Sign a document so a receiver can prove nobody touched it afterwards - the piece an e-invoice still misses.
roadmap.layoutTitle: The last few percent of layout
roadmap.layoutText: A public measure() helper, a heading across all columns, and a border that stays open where a box is split across pages.
roadmap.templatesText: An invoice, a report and a letter that work as they are, and come apart when you want your own.
roadmap.profilesText: Peppol and further country formats, on top of the Factur-X, ZUGFeRD and XRechnung profiles already supported.
roadmap.bidiText: Hebrew and Arabic already order correctly. The UAX #9 library behind that seam has not been touched since 2023 and ships no types, so it is going to be ours.

home.title: jasy - PDFs and XRechnung / ZUGFeRD e-invoices in TypeScript
home.description: Declarative PDFs - in Node or the browser, as functions, Vue or React components - and conformant XRechnung / ZUGFeRD e-invoices, checked with KoSIT and veraPDF. Pure TypeScript, no headless browser, no Java.
